concept.name: Independent component analysis
concept.definition: A linear latent-variable method that seeks components whose statistical dependence is minimized, often by maximizing non-Gaussianity.
concept.intuition: It is a learnable mapping or representation used to turn features into predictions or groups.
concept.mechanics: Center and whiten observations, optimize an unmixing matrix under an independence contrast, and transform later data using the fitted matrix.
concept.formula: S = W X, where rows of S are estimated independent sources
concept.failure_modes: Flexible models can fit noise, shift under new regimes, and conceal instability when tuning is repeated on the same validation data.
concept.misconceptions: Greater model complexity or in-sample accuracy does not by itself imply better out-of-sample trading results.
concept.example: ICA separates two mixed return drivers into components interpreted as market and sector shocks.
